chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Physical hazards of bus travel before the freeways
summary: Slow roads and poorly cushioned buses meant 500-mile hauls, hamburgers and arriving just in time to wash and dress, though a big enthusiastic crowd made you forget it.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: In traveling around, of course, again talking about the '20's and '30's, we didn't -- certainly didn't have the highway system that we have now, and cars didn't have quite the same kind of speed. How was just the physical activity of traveling? Was it really a big problem or did things work out pretty smoothly?

Well, I would say a lot of times it was a physical hazard, because of the fact that, as you mentioned before, we didn't have the highways that we have now, freeways and whatnot. It took you twice as long to get to your destination, you know, and sometimes riding in even the older buses that the bands used to ride on, I don't think they had enough shock absorbers of the right kind during those days when you'd have to take those bumpy roads, you know, and they'd shake you up, and sometimes the distance between the jobs that you play was so great, like 500 miles, you'd ride

the bus all day long, and only thing you'd do is get out to stretch and you stop to eat and get to one of the drive-ins and pick up hamburgers, and you get back in the bus and that shakes in your stomach and all, and by the time you get to the job, you'd have just about time enough to wash up and put your uniform on, and you'd be tired.

And you played all right, but sometimes you didn't play your best. However, if there was a huge crowd and an enthusiastic crowd, you'd forget your bumps and bruises, you know, and go on the play, especially if there were some pretty little girls.
Oh, yeah, that makes a difference, right.

You'd forget, man, and that would be it. And a lot of times you might play a job that you didn't have as many people, in the and -- that's when it would really show up, you know; you'd be tired, and you just say, "Well, I'm going to go and just play this gig tonight, but I don't feel good." You know, sometimes those things would happen. Of course, after all, you still were human, was (unintelligible).
